correctness.rationale: The reduction to the pentagon is proper because adjacent originals cannot both have apex colour and the replacement shadow sees both neighbours. The step sum is an odd multiple of three of magnitude at most five. The repaired apex proof compares projections in a common three-letter palette; summing over alternating blocks telescopes the internal changes, and the product of boundary factors is negative because the pentagon has odd length. The two sums are therefore opposite in that palette; the cofactor sign of the palette transposition gives exactly the stated normalization. Independently enumerated all 4^11 assignments and every one-coordinate neighbour with a state-membership index, verifying that both signs are nonempty and preserved on every edge, including all 2,280 apex edges. All-source unweighted shortest paths, without orbit pruning, confirm two sectors of 6,240 vertices and 22,620 edges each, with eccentricities 15/16/17 on 1,080/5,100/60 vertices per sector. The original degree census, fixed-apex connectivity and cross-edge counts agree. The 3-chromatic pentagon gives the standard obstruction to a 3-colouring of its Mycielskian, and the checked degeneracy order and spare-colour induction prove the stated five-colour threshold.
residual_risks: This is a proof and an exhaustive computational reproduction for this named graph, not a formal verification or a general Mycielski-graph theorem.
